questions.explanation: PowerShell's 'Resolve-DnsName' cmdlet performs DNS lookup resolution queries for specified names and record types.

questions.question: A network client cannot reach external internet sites, but can ping other machines on the same local subnet. Which diagnostic check should be performed first using command line tools?
options: A) Ping the default gateway IP address
B) Flush the local ARP cache
questions.explanation: Pinging the default gateway verifies local router reachability, which is required to forward packets to external subnets.

questions.question: Which parameter for the 'ipconfig' command forces a Windows host to re-register its host name and IP address with configured DNS servers?
questions.explanation: 'ipconfig /registerdns' initiates manual dynamic registration for DNS names and IP addresses configured on the client.

questions.question: A user is experiencing poor performance on a Linux system. The technician wants to display real-time active socket connections and listening ports. Which modern Linux command replaces netstat?
questions.explanation: The 'ss' utility (socket statistics) is the modern replacement for 'netstat' in Linux distributions.

questions.question: Which command clears all static and dynamic entries stored in the Windows ARP cache?
questions.explanation: The command 'arp -d *' (or 'arp -d' in administrative prompt) flushes dynamic IP-to-MAC address entries from the ARP table.

questions.question: A computer receives ICMP time-exceeded messages during path discovery. Which command relies on incremental Time To Live (TTL) adjustments to trace path hops?
questions.explanation: 'tracert' sends packets with incrementing TTL values starting at 1, capturing ICMP 'Time Exceeded' messages from routers along the path.

questions.question: A technician needs to check basic ICMP echo connectivity in Linux. By default, how does the Linux 'ping' command behave differently from Windows ping?
options: A) Linux ping continues sending packets infinitely until stopped manually (Ctrl+C)
B) Linux ping defaults to 4 packets only
C) Linux ping requires root privileges to execute
D) Linux ping uses UDP port 53 by default
questions.explanation: Unlike Windows ping (which sends 4 echo requests by default), Linux ping runs continuously until interrupted unless specified with the '-c' count flag.

questions.question: Which command options in nslookup allow a technician to explicitly specify a server target such as 8.8.8.8 to test name resolution?
questions.explanation: Executing 'nslookup [domain_name] [DNS_server_IP]' directs the query to a specific DNS server (e.g., 'nslookup company.com 8.8.8.8').

questions.question: A technician suspects that a workstation has a bad default gateway configuration. Which command output on a Windows machine displays the default gateway IP?
questions.explanation: 'ipconfig' displays IPv4/IPv6 addresses, subnet masks, and the Default Gateway assigned to active network adapters.

questions.question: Which diagnostic command tests local loopback functionality on an IP host without sending traffic over physical wire?
questions.explanation: Pinging 127.0.0.1 (IPv4 loopback) or ::1 (IPv6 loopback) verifies that the local TCP/IP protocol stack is installed and functioning.

questions.question: Which netstat switch displays network statistics organized by protocol (e.g., IP, ICMP, TCP, UDP)?
questions.explanation: The '-s' option displays per-protocol statistics for TCP, UDP, ICMP, and IP protocols.

questions.question: A network admin needs to trace path hops on a Linux server using ICMP instead of the default UDP packets. Which parameter should be used with traceroute?
questions.explanation: The '-I' switch forces Linux traceroute to use ICMP ECHO requests instead of default UDP probes.

questions.question: Which Windows command can be used to display or alter NetBIOS over TCP/IP (NBT) name resolution tables?
questions.explanation: 'nbtstat' displays NetBIOS over TCP/IP statistics and name tables.

questions.question: A technician wants to query a specific mail server record (MX) using nslookup. What sequence of commands should be entered into the interactive nslookup prompt?
options: A) set type=MX followed by domain name entry
questions.explanation: Inside the nslookup interactive shell, 'set type=MX' instructs the utility to query Mail Exchanger records for subsequent domain lookups.

questions.question: Which Linux command displays modern default gateway routes and network path information?
questions.explanation: 'ip route show' (or 'ip route') displays routing table entries on Linux.

questions.question: A user's host is sending traffic to an incorrect next-hop router. Which utility can add a static route directly to the host routing table?
questions.explanation: The 'route' command (e.g., 'route add') is used to view and modify network routing tables.

questions.question: Which command line utility displays the host name of the current computer operating system session?
questions.explanation: The 'hostname' command prints the configured name of the local computer system.

questions.question: A technician executes 'ping -f -l 1472 192.168.1.1' on Windows. What purpose do these parameters serve?
options: A) Test for Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) packet fragmentation limits
B) Send fast ICMP loops with 1472 retries
C) Flood the gateway with 1472 small packets
questions.explanation: The '-f' flag sets the 'Don't Fragment' bit, and '-l 1472' sets payload buffer size. This combination tests MTU threshold size without allowing packet fragmentation.

questions.question: Which Linux DNS lookup tool is simpler than 'dig' and outputs basic IP address mappings by default?
questions.explanation: The 'host' command in Linux provides quick domain-to-IP lookups in a concise format.

questions.question: What does a ping response showing 'Destination Host Unreachable' indicate?
options: A) The local system or local router cannot discover an IP route or ARP entry to the target host
B) The target host answered but refused TCP connection
C) DNS resolution completed, but port 80 is blocked
D) The local physical cable is disconnected
questions.explanation: 'Destination Host Unreachable' indicates that the default gateway or local host could not find a path or resolve the MAC address (via ARP) for the destination IP.

questions.question: What does a ping result showing 'Request Timed Out' typically imply?
options: A) The target host did not respond within the default timeout period (often dropped by firewall or powered off)
B) The local IP address is missing
C) The DNS server is misconfigured
D) The network cable has high voltage
questions.explanation: 'Request Timed Out' indicates echo requests were sent, but no echo reply arrived within the timeout interval, commonly due to strict host firewalls blocking ICMP or an offline device.

questions.question: Which command forces a Windows network adapter to release its active IPv6 address configuration back to the network router/DHCPv6 server?
questions.explanation: 'ipconfig /release6' specifically releases IPv6 address leases obtained via DHCPv6.

questions.question: Which command renews IPv6 network leases on Windows?
questions.explanation: 'ipconfig /renew6' requests a new IPv6 configuration from a DHCPv6 server.

questions.question: A technician needs to find the process ID (PID) associated with a rogue port listening on a Linux machine. Which command combination displays listening ports with process names and PIDs?
questions.explanation: 'ss -tulpn' (TCP, UDP, Listening, Processes, Numeric) displays listening sockets along with process names and PIDs on Linux.

questions.question: A Windows user cannot resolve hostnames. The technician runs 'nslookup server1' and receives 'DNS request timed out.' Which commands can help diagnose or fix the issue? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Pinging the DNS server IP checks basic network connectivity to the server, and flushing the DNS cache removes invalid or stale entries.

questions.question: Which Linux terminal tool is commonly used to perform real-time continuous path tracing combining ping and traceroute statistics into an interactive view?
questions.explanation: 'mtr' (My TraceRoute) is a popular Linux tool that continuously tracks network path hops and live packet loss stats.

questions.question: A technician wants to view detailed system information, including OS version, network card details, hotfixes, and domain membership via Windows CLI. Which command should be run?
questions.explanation: The 'systeminfo' command outputs detailed operating system configurations, hardware specifications, and network interface properties.

questions.question: Which command line sequence in PowerShell resets all TCP/IP stack configurations to default state on a malfunctioning Windows computer?
questions.explanation: 'netsh int ip reset' resets the Windows TCP/IP stack registry keys back to default factory states, resolving corrupt protocol issues.

questions.question: A technician installs a brand new unformatted NVMe SSD into a Windows 11 workstation. When opening Disk Management, the drive appears as 'Unknown' and 'Not Initialized'. What is the first step required before the drive can be partitioned?
options: A) Format the drive with NTFS
B) Initialize the disk with a partition style (MBR or GPT)
C) Convert the disk to a dynamic disk
D) Assign a drive letter to the unallocated space
questions.explanation: Before a new physical disk can be partitioned or formatted in Windows, it must first be initialized with a partition style such as MBR or GPT.

questions.question: A technician wants to configure software-based RAID 1 (mirroring) across two secondary hard drives in Windows Disk Management. What conversion must be performed on the basic disks before creating the mirrored volume?
options: A) Convert them to dynamic disks
B) Convert them to exFAT format
C) Convert the partition table to MBR
D) Convert the disks to Virtual Hard Disks (VHD)
questions.explanation: Advanced software volume types like spanned, striped (RAID 0), and mirrored (RAID 1) volumes require basic disks to be converted to dynamic disks.

questions.question: A user needs to expand an existing C: volume on a Windows system using contiguous unallocated space located immediately to its right. Which Disk Management feature should be used?
options: D) Change Drive Letter and Paths
questions.explanation: The 'Extend Volume' feature allows administrators to append contiguous unallocated space to an existing partition without data loss.

questions.question: When initializing a 4 TB secondary hard drive in Windows Disk Management, which partition style must be chosen to utilize the full storage capacity as a single volume?
questions.explanation: MBR supports maximum disk sizes of 2 TB. To address disk space greater than 2 TB, GPT (GUID Partition Table) must be used.

questions.question: What occurs when converting a basic disk containing existing data volumes into a dynamic disk in Windows?
options: A) Existing partitions are converted to simple volumes without data loss
B) All existing data on the drive is immediately erased
C) The file system is automatically reformatted to FAT32
D) The disk is forcibly converted from GPT to MBR
questions.explanation: Converting a basic disk to a dynamic disk preserves existing partitions and turns them into simple dynamic volumes without destroying data.

questions.question: What is required prior to converting a dynamic disk back into a basic disk in Windows Disk Management?
options: A) Delete all dynamic volumes on the drive
C) Disable BitLocker on the system drive
D) Convert the file system scheme to exFAT
questions.explanation: To convert a dynamic disk back to a basic disk using Disk Management, all existing volumes on the disk must first be deleted, which erases all data on the disk.

questions.question: A technician needs to extend a basic partition on a disk. Which of the following conditions must be met? (Select TWO)
options: A) The unallocated space must be directly to the right of the partition (contiguous)
B) The target partition must be formatted with NTFS or ReFS
C) The disk must be connected via USB 3.0 or higher
D) The partition must be configured as an MBR primary boot volume
E) The disk must be formatted with exFAT
questions.explanation: On basic disks, extending a partition requires contiguous unallocated space directly following (to the right of) the target volume, and the volume must use an extendable file system like NTFS or ReFS.

questions.question: Which MMC (Microsoft Management Console) snap-in filename or tool opens the Windows Disk Management graphical interface? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: 'diskmgmt.msc' opens Disk Management directly, while Computer Management ('compmgmt.msc') includes Disk Management under the Storage tree.

questions.question: Which partition types can be created on a basic disk initialized with the MBR partition style? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: MBR basic disks use standard partition structures: Primary and Extended partitions. Advanced volume types (Striped, Spanned, Mirrored) require dynamic disks.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of primary partitions supported on a basic disk initialized with MBR without creating an extended partition?
questions.explanation: MBR partition tables support a maximum of 4 primary partitions, or 3 primary partitions plus 1 extended partition containing logical drives.

questions.question: How many primary partitions are supported natively under the GPT (GUID Partition Table) partition style in Windows?
questions.explanation: GPT supports up to 128 primary partitions natively in Windows without requiring extended partitions.

questions.question: A technician wants to combine non-contiguous unallocated spaces across two separate physical hard drives into one single drive letter without fault tolerance. What volume type must be created on dynamic disks?
questions.explanation: A Spanned volume combines unallocated space from multiple physical dynamic drives into a single logical drive letter.

questions.question: Which dynamic volume type provides fault tolerance by keeping an exact duplicate of data on two separate physical drives?
questions.explanation: Mirrored volumes (software RAID 1) mirror data identically across two physical disks to provide redundancy.

questions.question: A technician creates a new partition using unallocated space on a newly initialized basic drive. What step is necessary so users can read and write files on it?
options: A) Format the volume with a supported file system and assign a drive letter
B) Convert the disk to dynamic
C) Run chkdsk /r on the unallocated space
questions.explanation: After creating a partition, it must be formatted with a file system (such as NTFS or exFAT) and assigned a drive letter to be accessible to the operating system.

questions.question: Which command-line interface tool in Windows allows administrators to manage partitions, initialize disks, and convert basic disks to dynamic disks?
questions.explanation: 'diskpart' is the command-line disk management utility capable of partitioning, formatting, initializing, and converting disks.

questions.question: A technician attempts to extend a volume on Disk 0 using unallocated space on Disk 1. What will Windows Disk Management do to Disk 0 and Disk 1 if the action is confirmed?
options: A) Convert both disks to Dynamic Disks and create a Spanned Volume
B) Format Disk 1 with exFAT automatically
C) Convert both disks to GPT partition style
D) Reject the change stating basic disks cannot hold unallocated space
questions.explanation: Extending a partition across multiple physical hard drives converts basic disks to dynamic disks to form a spanned volume.

questions.question: A technician moves a dynamic disk from a decommissioned Windows PC into a user's desktop. In Disk Management, the drive status is displayed as 'Foreign'. How can the technician gain access to the data?
options: A) Right-click the disk and select 'Import Foreign Disks'
B) Initialize the disk as MBR
C) Convert the disk to a basic disk immediately
D) Format the drive with NTFS
questions.explanation: A dynamic disk transferred from another host displays as 'Foreign'. Selecting 'Import Foreign Disks' brings the existing dynamic volumes online without destroying data.

questions.question: Which option in Windows Disk Management decreases the space utilized by an existing volume to create unallocated space?
questions.explanation: 'Shrink Volume' reduces the size of an existing partition, turning the freed area into unallocated space.

questions.question: A secondary internal hard drive displays a status of 'Offline' in Disk Management. Which action will reactivate the drive?
options: A) Right-click the disk and select 'Online'
C) Convert the disk to MBR
D) Rebuild the master boot record
questions.explanation: Right-clicking an offline disk header in Disk Management and selecting 'Online' brings the drive back into service.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of choosing the GPT partition style over MBR when initializing a new hard drive?
options: A) Supports volumes larger than 2 TB and includes backup partition tables
B) Compatible with 16-bit legacy operating systems
C) Provides faster network connection throughput
D) Removes the necessity to format volumes
questions.explanation: GPT supports volume sizes up to 9.4 ZB (well over the 2 TB limit of MBR) and stores duplicate header data for error recovery.

questions.question: What disk status is displayed in Disk Management when a dynamic disk experiences I/O hardware failures or corrupted volume headers?
questions.explanation: An 'Unreadable' status indicates hardware failure, I/O errors, or dynamic disk database corruption.

questions.question: A technician needs to expand an existing volume using non-adjacent unallocated space on the same physical drive. Which disk layout type is required?
questions.explanation: Dynamic disks allow simple volumes to be extended across non-contiguous blocks on the same physical drive.

questions.question: When creating a volume on a basic disk in Disk Management, which feature attaches the volume to an empty directory on an existing NTFS file system instead of assigning a letter?
options: A) Mount in the following empty NTFS folder
B) Assign the following drive letter
C) Do not assign a drive letter or path
D) Create a Spanned Mount point
questions.explanation: Windows allows mounting a volume inside an empty folder on an existing NTFS formatted partition using drive paths.

questions.question: Which dynamic volume type stripes data blocks across two or more physical drives to increase performance but provides no fault tolerance?
questions.explanation: Striped volumes (software RAID 0) interleave data across disks to optimize throughput, but if any drive fails, all data is lost.

questions.question: A technician initializes a drive using the MBR partition style and creates an extended partition. How many logical drives can be created inside the extended partition?
options: A) Multiple drives (limited primarily by available drive letters and system resources)
questions.explanation: An extended partition on an MBR disk can be subdivided into multiple logical drives, limited by available OS drive letters and system resources.

questions.question: Which option in Disk Management designates a primary partition on an MBR disk as the bootable partition containing startup files for legacy systems?
questions.explanation: 'Mark Partition as Active' identifies the primary partition that contains system boot files used by legacy BIOS system configurations.

questions.question: A system administrator installs an 8 TB hard drive on a modern Windows 11 system with UEFI. Which partition style should be selected during initialization?
questions.explanation: UEFI boot compatibility and storage drives larger than 2 TB require the GPT (GUID Partition Table) partition style.

questions.question: A technician needs to reassign a secondary partition's drive letter from D: to S:. Where in Windows can this be completed using built-in administrative tools?
questions.explanation: Right-clicking a volume in Disk Management and choosing 'Change Drive Letter and Paths' allows reassigning drive letters.

questions.question: What is a major potential issue when converting a basic disk to a dynamic disk on a dual-boot machine running non-Windows operating systems?
options: A) Non-Windows operating systems may be unable to read dynamic disk volumes
B) The drive automatically reformats to MBR
C) Dynamic disks force BitLocker encryption automatically
D) Drive size is permanently restricted to 32 GB
questions.explanation: Dynamic disks use a proprietary Microsoft logical structure that non-Windows or older boot environments often cannot read.

questions.question: A technician opens Disk Management and sees a drive listed as 'Not Initialized' alongside a red down-arrow icon. What visual indicator represents the unformatted drive space?
options: A) Black bar indicating unallocated space
B) Dark blue bar indicating primary partition
C) Green bar indicating extended partition
D) Light blue bar indicating logical drive
questions.explanation: Unallocated space on an uninitialized drive is visually represented by a black status bar.

questions.question: In Windows Disk Management, what color indicates a primary partition on a standard basic disk by default?
questions.explanation: By default in Disk Management, dark blue indicates a primary partition, black indicates unallocated space, and light blue indicates a logical drive.

questions.question: Which command-line sequence in diskpart initializes Disk 1 with GPT, creates a primary partition, and performs a quick NTFS format?
options: A) select disk 1 -> convert gpt -> create partition primary -> format fs=ntfs quick
B) format fs=ntfs quick -> select disk 1 -> create partition primary
C) convert dynamic -> select disk 1 -> assign letter=E
D) attach vhd -> convert mbr -> shrink desired=5000
questions.explanation: The proper order in diskpart requires selecting the target disk, converting to the desired partition style, creating the partition, and formatting with a file system.

questions.question: A technician attempts to extend the C: volume on a basic disk, but the 'Extend Volume' option is grayed out in Disk Management. What is the most common cause?
options: A) Unallocated space is not located directly to the right (contiguous) of the C: volume
B) The C: volume is formatted using the NTFS file system
C) The machine is connected to an Active Directory domain
D) The user is running Windows 11 Home Edition
questions.explanation: Basic disks require unallocated space to be contiguous and positioned directly to the right of the target volume for the 'Extend Volume' option to function.

questions.question: Which component of the GPT partition layout resides at sector LBA 0 to prevent legacy tools from accidentally overwriting GPT structure?
questions.explanation: GPT includes a Protective MBR at LBA 0 so legacy partition management tools treat the disk as occupied rather than empty.

questions.question: What system requirement must be met prior to converting an MBR system disk to GPT using the native MBR2GPT.exe utility?
options: A) The system motherboard firmware must support UEFI boot mode
B) The hard drive must be converted to a dynamic disk first
C) The system partition must be formatted with FAT32
D) The disk must contain 4 existing primary partitions
questions.explanation: Converting an MBR system drive to GPT requires UEFI firmware support to ensure the machine can boot after conversion.

questions.question: A technician replaces a failed hard drive in a software RAID 1 (mirrored) setup. What steps should be taken in Disk Management to restore disk redundancy?
options: A) Initialize the replacement disk, right-click the existing mirror volume, and select 'Add Mirror'
B) Convert the replacement disk to MBR and format it with FAT32
C) Run chkdsk /f on the new disk
questions.explanation: To re-establish software RAID 1, the new disk is initialized and added as a mirror to the surviving dynamic volume.

questions.question: Which storage layout dynamic disk type combines unallocated space from multiple physical hard drives into a single continuous logical volume without data mirroring?
questions.explanation: A Spanned volume merges unallocated space from two or more physical drives into one larger logical volume.

questions.question: What status is displayed in Disk Management while a newly added physical disk synchronizes data in a software RAID 1 configuration?
questions.explanation: While data is copying to mirror the second disk, Disk Management displays the 'Resynching' status.

questions.question: Which command sequence converts basic Disk 2 to dynamic using the diskpart CLI utility?
questions.explanation: In diskpart, selecting the disk (select disk 2) and running convert dynamic switches the disk from basic to dynamic.

questions.question: Why can dynamic disks NOT be created on standard external USB flash drives in Windows?
options: A) Windows does not support dynamic disk layout on removable storage media
B) Removable flash drives only support hardware RAID 5
C) Removable flash drives are limited to 32 GB total size
D) USB drives cannot be formatted using NTFS
questions.explanation: Windows explicitly prevents creating dynamic disk structures on removable drives like USB flash drives.

questions.question: A technician needs to create a virtual hard disk file (.vhd) and mount it as a local disk. Which built-in utility provides a graphical menu under 'Action' to create and attach VHD files?
questions.explanation: Disk Management has built-in Action menu options to 'Create VHD' and 'Attach VHD'.

questions.question: What primary purpose does an Extended Partition serve on a basic disk initialized with MBR?
options: A) It acts as a container to hold multiple logical drives
B) It automatically mirrors data for disaster recovery
C) It speeds up read/write access times for swap files
D) It converts the MBR disk to a GPT disk automatically
questions.explanation: An extended partition overcomes the MBR 4-primary partition limit by acting as a container that hosts multiple logical drives.

questions.question: A technician shrinks volume D: to create space for volume C:, but the resulting unallocated space sits between volume D: and volume E:. Why can volume C: NOT be extended on a basic disk?
options: A) The unallocated space is not adjacent to volume C:
B) Volume C: must be formatted with exFAT
C) Volume C: must be moved to an external USB drive
D) MBR drives do not support shrinking partitions
questions.explanation: On basic disks, the unallocated space must be directly contiguous to the right of the target volume.

questions.question: What happens to stored files when a simple volume on a dynamic disk is extended using non-adjacent space on the same physical drive?
options: A) Files remain intact without data loss
B) All files are immediately wiped
C) The volume enters an Offline state
questions.explanation: Extending a dynamic volume expands the logical drive size while retaining all existing data.

questions.question: Which Disk Management status indicates that a volume is online, properly formatted, and operating normally without detected file system errors?
questions.explanation: The 'Healthy' status confirms that the volume is accessible and functioning properly.

questions.question: Which modern Windows storage management feature allows combining multiple physical drives into virtual pools with redundancy options, replacing legacy Dynamic Disks?
questions.explanation: Storage Spaces is Microsoft's modern software-defined storage feature that groups physical drives into pools to create resilient virtual disks.

questions.question: A technician connects a new internal hard drive. Disk Management shows 'Disk 1' with a solid black header bar across the entire disk layout. What does this black bar represent?
questions.explanation: A black bar in Disk Management indicates unallocated space that has not been assigned to a volume or partition.

questions.question: Which built-in command-line tool converts an MBR system partition to GPT without wiping or deleting data on the drive?
questions.explanation: MBR2GPT.exe converts an MBR formatted disk to GPT without modifying or deleting data on the disk.

questions.question: What happens if one physical drive fails in a 2-disk dynamic software Striped volume (RAID 0)?
options: A) Total data loss occurs across the volume
B) The remaining drive automatically rebuilds the missing data
C) Data remains readable on the surviving drive
D) The volume automatically converts into a simple basic disk
questions.explanation: Striped volumes (RAID 0) provide high speed by striping data across drives without redundancy. If one drive fails, all volume data is lost.

questions.question: A technician installs a new physical hard drive. Which three basic setup tasks must be completed in order to prepare the drive for storage? (Select THREE)
options: A) Initialize the disk with a partition style (MBR/GPT)
C) Format the volume with a file system
E) Configure an incoming VPN connection
questions.explanation: Preparing a new disk requires initializing the disk (MBR or GPT), creating volumes/partitions, and formatting them with a file system (NTFS/FAT32/exFAT).

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A standard user in a Windows environment attempts to install a third-party application. A User Account Control (UAC) dialog appears on the screen. What is required for the installation to proceed?
options: A) The standard user must enter their own user password.
B) An administrator must provide administrative credentials.
C) The user must restart the system in Safe Mode.
D) The application must be moved to the Program Files directory.
questions.explanation: When a standard user attempts an action requiring elevated privileges, UAC prompts for administrative credentials (credential prompt).

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A user moves a folder from C:\Reports to C:\Archive on the same NTFS volume. Which statement correctly describes the NTFS permissions of the moved folder?
options: A) The folder inherits the permissions of C:\Archive.
B) The folder retains its original permissions from C:\Reports.
C) The folder loses all permissions and becomes accessible to Everyone.
D) The folder permissions revert to default administrative read-only.
questions.explanation: Moving a file or folder within the same NTFS volume retains its original permissions. (Copying or moving across volumes causes it to inherit target folder permissions).

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A technician copies a file from an NTFS partition on Disk 0 to an NTFS partition on Disk 1. What happens to the file's NTFS permissions?
options: A) The file retains its original explicit permissions.
B) The file inherits the permissions of the destination folder on Disk 1.
C) The file becomes read-only and unencrypted.
D) The file permissions are stripped entirely.
questions.explanation: Copying a file to any location (same or different partition) causes the copy to inherit the target folder's permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A share permission grants a user 'Full Control', but the NTFS permission on the same folder grants 'Read' access. When accessing the folder over the network, what is the user's effective permission?
questions.explanation: When Share permissions and NTFS permissions combine for network access, the most restrictive permission applies. Read is more restrictive than Full Control.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which MMC console utility snap-in is used to edit Local Group Policies on a standalone Windows Professional or Enterprise machine?
questions.explanation: gpedit.msc opens the Local Group Policy Editor.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: An administrator wants to hide a shared folder named Confidential from appearing in network browsing lists while keeping it accessible to users who type the exact path. How should the share name be configured?
questions.explanation: Appending a dollar sign ($) to the end of a share name creates an administrative/hidden share that does not appear in network browsing.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A user is explicitly granted 'Full Control' NTFS permissions to a folder via their user account. However, they are also a member of a group that has an explicit 'Deny Read' permission set on the same folder. What is the user's effective access?
questions.explanation: In NTFS permissions, an explicit Deny permission always overrides explicit or inherited Allow permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which level of User Account Control (UAC) notification darkens the desktop and prompts for confirmation only when apps make changes, but NOT when the user makes Windows settings changes?
options: B) Notify me only when apps try to make changes to my computer (default)
C) Notify me only when apps try to make changes (do not dim my desktop)
questions.explanation: The default UAC setting notifies only when applications attempt to make changes to the system while dimming the desktop (Secure Desktop).

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which of the following NTFS permissions allows a user to open files, read content, view attributes, but prevents them from modifying or deleting files? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Both Read and Read & Execute permit viewing file contents and attributes without allowing edits, writes, or deletions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A user accesses a file locally by logging directly into a Windows machine. Which permissions determine their actual file system access?
options: C) The most restrictive combination of Share and NTFS permissions
D) User Account Control elevation permissions only
questions.explanation: Share permissions only apply when accessing resources across a network connection. Local access relies solely on NTFS permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: An administrator wants to force local account lockout policies after 5 failed login attempts. Which tool should be used on a standalone Windows 11 workstation?
questions.explanation: secpol.msc (Local Security Policy) is used to configure Account Lockout Policies and Password Policies on non-domain Windows systems.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which Command Prompt utility forces an immediate refresh and re-application of Local Group Policy settings without restarting the computer?
questions.explanation: gpupdate /force updates and refreshes Group Policy settings immediately.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which standard administrative shared folder path allows access to the root of drive C: across a local network for system administrators?
questions.explanation: \\computername\C$ is the default hidden administrative share pointing to the root of the C drive.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What is the primary function of the Secure Desktop feature in Windows User Account Control (UAC)?
options: A) It prevents untrusted background software from manipulating the UAC prompt.
B) It encrypts the user's hard drive using BitLocker.
C) It enforces complex password criteria.
D) It blocks network traffic on port 445.
questions.explanation: The Secure Desktop dims the background and isolates the UAC dialog so malicious code cannot simulate user mouse clicks or keystrokes.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A user belongs to Group A (NTFS Read) and Group B (NTFS Write) for the same folder. What is the user's effective local NTFS permission on that folder?
questions.explanation: NTFS Allow permissions are cumulative. Belonging to multiple groups combines their allowed rights (Read + Write = Read & Write).

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which permission level is available under Share Permissions in Windows? (Select THREE)
questions.explanation: Share permissions only have three permission options: Read, Change, and Full Control.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: An administrator wants to prevent child folders from inheriting permissions from their parent folder. Where in Windows File Explorer can this option be disabled?
options: A) Folder Properties -> Security tab -> Advanced -> Disable Inheritance
B) Folder Properties -> General tab -> Advanced Attributes
C) Folder Properties -> Sharing tab -> Advanced Sharing
D) Control Panel -> User Accounts -> Turn off Inheritance
questions.explanation: Permission inheritance is configured under the Security tab -> Advanced Security Settings -> Disable Inheritance.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which command-line utility displays the summary of applied Group Policy settings (Resultant Set of Policy) for a logged-in user and computer?
questions.explanation: gpresult displays the Resultant Set of Policy (RSoP) information for a user or computer.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What difference distinguishes the NTFS 'Modify' permission from the NTFS 'Full Control' permission?
options: A) Modify allows editing files but does not allow changing permissions or taking ownership.
B) Modify allows deleting files, whereas Full Control does not.
C) Full Control is only available over the network.
D) Modify prevents users from reading subdirectories.
questions.explanation: Modify permits creating, editing, and deleting files, but only Full Control allows changing file permissions and taking file ownership.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A technician moves a file from D:\Data (NTFS) to E:\Data (NTFS). What happens to the file's NTFS permissions?
options: A) The file inherits the permissions of E:\Data.
B) The file retains its original permissions from D:\Data.
C) The file requires administrator elevation to open.
D) The file permissions revert to default system read-only.
questions.explanation: Moving a file across different NTFS volumes acts like a copy/delete operation, so the file inherits the destination folder's permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which command-line tool allows users and administrators to view and modify NTFS Access Control Lists (ACLs) on files and folders?
questions.explanation: icacls (and legacy cacls) is the command-line utility used to view and modify NTFS permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What occurs when a file is moved from an NTFS drive volume to a FAT32 USB drive?
options: A) All NTFS permissions are lost because FAT32 does not support file permissions.
B) The NTFS permissions are preserved inside a hidden FAT32 header.
C) The move fails because FAT32 cannot accept files from NTFS volumes.
D) UAC prompts for an administrative password.
questions.explanation: FAT32 does not support security access control lists (ACLs) or NTFS permissions, so moving files to FAT32 strips all permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which Administrative Share points directly to the default Windows installation system folder (e.g., C:\Windows)?
questions.explanation: The ADMIN$ share points directly to the system root directory (typically C:\Windows).

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: An administrator wants to disable UAC entirely on a workstation for testing. Which UAC slider position turns off UAC prompts?
questions.explanation: Setting the UAC slider to 'Never notify' disables UAC prompt elevations.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A share has Share Permissions of 'Read' for Everyone, and NTFS permissions of 'Modify' for Users. When connected remotely, what can a user in the Users group do?
questions.explanation: Effective remote permission is the most restrictive between Share and NTFS permissions. Share (Read) is more restrictive than NTFS (Modify), restricting access to Read-only.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which command-line command lists all active shared resources on a local Windows computer?
questions.explanation: net share displays all shares configured on the local system.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which command connects a client machine to a remote network share \\Server\Data using drive letter Z:?
questions.explanation: net use Z: \\Server\Data maps a network share to drive letter Z:.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which local group policy folder allows administrators to configure password age, complexity, and account lockout thresholds?
options: A) Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Account Policies
B) User Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Desktop
C) Computer Configuration -> System -> User Profiles
D) User Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Account Lockout
questions.explanation: Account Policies (Password Policy and Account Lockout Policy) are located under Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A user needs to grant permission for another user to view and run executable programs in a folder without granting write access. Which NTFS permission should be assigned?
questions.explanation: 'Read & Execute' allows reading file contents and executing applications while preventing file modification.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What is the result of assigning 'Deny Write' explicit NTFS permissions to a folder for a specific user?
options: A) The user cannot write to or modify files in the folder regardless of group Allow permissions.
B) The user can write to files if they belong to the Administrators group.
C) The user can write to files over the network if share permissions allow it.
D) The user is granted read-only access to parent folders only.
questions.explanation: Explicit Deny rules take precedence over all Allow rules, blocking write capability entirely.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which tab in a shared folder's Properties dialog box is used to configure NTFS permissions?
questions.explanation: NTFS permissions are managed on the 'Security' tab, while network share permissions are managed on the 'Sharing' tab.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which tab in a folder's Properties dialog box is used to set up basic network share permissions?
questions.explanation: Network sharing settings and Share permissions are configured on the 'Sharing' tab.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: When an administrator creates a new folder within an existing directory, what NTFS permissions does the new folder initially receive?
options: A) It inherits permissions from its parent directory.
B) It receives Full Control for Everyone.
C) It has no permissions assigned until specified.
D) It receives Read-only access for Administrators.
questions.explanation: By default, new subfolders inherit permissions from their parent folder.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What occurs when a standard user logs into Windows and launches an application that does NOT require elevation?
options: A) The application runs with standard user rights without a UAC prompt.
B) UAC prompts for the user's standard password.
C) UAC prompts for administrator credentials.
D) The app runs with full administrative privileges automatically.
questions.explanation: Applications that do not perform system-wide changes run directly under the standard user's limited token without triggering UAC.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which windows tool enables technicians to audit logon failures and success events via Local Security Policy?
questions.explanation: Audit Policies in secpol.msc allow logging successful and failed logon attempts to the Windows Security Event Log.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: An administrator wants to ensure that share permissions do not limit NTFS permissions for remote network users. Which share permission setting should be applied?
options: A) Grant Full Control to Everyone at the share level, then secure files using NTFS permissions.
B) Grant Read-only share permissions to Everyone.
C) Disable NTFS permissions and use Share permissions exclusively.
D) Remove the Everyone group from the share permission list.
questions.explanation: Best practice is to grant Full Control at the share level, allowing granular NTFS permissions to control effective access.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What UAC behavior occurs when an administrative user executes a task requiring elevated privileges under default UAC settings?
options: A) A consent prompt asks the administrator to click 'Yes' to proceed.
B) A credential prompt requires re-entering the admin password.
C) The action is silently blocked without notification.
D) Windows automatically reboots into Safe Mode.
questions.explanation: Administrators operate with a split token; when elevating, UAC displays a Consent prompt ('Yes'/'No') rather than requiring a password.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which default share permission is assigned when creating a basic shared folder via Advanced Sharing in Windows?
questions.explanation: When using Advanced Sharing in Windows, the default share permission granted is Read access to the Everyone group.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which of the following describes the effect of explicit NTFS permissions vs. inherited NTFS permissions?
options: A) Explicit permissions applied directly to an object take precedence over inherited permissions from a parent folder.
B) Inherited permissions always override explicit permissions.
C) Explicit permissions are deleted when a folder is renamed.
D) Inherited permissions only apply to administrative users.
questions.explanation: Explicit permissions assigned directly on a file or folder take precedence over permissions inherited from higher-level folders.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: An administrator wants to restrict local users from running specific Control Panel applets using Local Group Policy. Which policy node should be edited?
options: A) User Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Control Panel
B) Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> System Services
C) User Configuration -> Software Settings -> Network Shares
D) Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Network Connections
questions.explanation: User-specific interface restrictions like Control Panel access are governed under User Configuration -> Administrative Templates.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which share permission allows users to read, execute, create, edit, and delete files inside a network share, but does NOT allow changing share permissions?
questions.explanation: The 'Change' share permission allows reading, editing, adding, and deleting files, but not modifying permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A technician needs to give a user the ability to traverse subfolders, list contents, and run apps, but NOT modify file contents. Which NTFS permission is best suited?
questions.explanation: Read & Execute permits traversing folders, reading contents, and executing applications.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which security setting in Local Security Policy (secpol.msc) locks an account after a specified number of incorrect password attempts?
questions.explanation: The 'Account lockout threshold' defines how many failed login attempts trigger an account lockout.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: If a user is granted Share 'Change' permission and NTFS 'Full Control' permission, what actions can they perform over the network? (Select TWO)
options: D) Take ownership of the file
questions.explanation: Because Share permissions limit access to 'Change', remote users can modify and delete files, but cannot take ownership or alter security permissions (which require Share Full Control).

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What happens when an explicit Allow permission conflicts with an inherited Deny permission on an NTFS folder?
options: A) The explicit Allow permission takes precedence.
B) The inherited Deny permission takes precedence.
C) The permissions cancel out, denying access.
D) Windows forces the folder to convert to FAT32.
questions.explanation: Explicit permissions (whether Allow or Deny) take precedence over inherited permissions.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: What is the purpose of the PRINT$ administrative share in a Windows networking environment?
options: A) To share printer drivers automatically across the network for connecting clients
B) To log all printed documents to an encrypted text file
C) To store temporary print queues during network outages
D) To restrict unauthorized users from printing color documents
questions.explanation: The PRINT$ administrative share holds printer drivers that are automatically downloaded when client computers connect to shared printers.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which User Account Control (UAC) setting notifies users only when applications attempt to make changes, but does NOT dim the desktop?
options: A) Notify me only when apps try to make changes (do not dim my desktop)
C) Notify me only when I make changes to Windows settings
questions.explanation: The third UAC slider setting presents elevation prompts without switching to the dim secure desktop.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A technician needs to grant write permissions to a folder while ensuring the user cannot delete the folder or alter permissions. Which NTFS permission level is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The Write permission allows creating and writing to files, whereas Modify adds deletion rights and Full Control adds permission management.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Which MMC console snap-in manages local user accounts and local groups on Windows Professional and Enterprise editions?
questions.explanation: lusrmgr.msc opens Local Users and Groups.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: A folder has explicit NTFS permissions assigned. If an administrator checks 'Replace all child object permission entries with inheritable permission entries from this object', what happens to subfolders?
options: A) All explicit permissions on subfolders are overwritten by the parent folder's permissions.
B) Subfolders maintain their custom permissions alongside inherited ones.
C) The subfolders are automatically encrypted.
D) The subfolders become hidden administrative shares.
questions.explanation: Checking this option replaces explicit permissions on all child objects with inherited permissions from the parent object.

questions.objective: 2.6 – Given a scenario, implement procedures for basic small office/home office (SOHO) malware removal
questions.question: Correctly order the seven-step malware removal process
items: Enable System Restore and create a restore point
answer: Enable System Restore and create a restore point

questions.question: Match each suspicious process observed in Windows Task Manager to its corresponding threat description: (1) svchost.exe running from AppData\Local\Temp, (2) lsass.exe consuming 99% CPU with no digital signature, (3) powershell.exe executing encoded base64 commands at startup.
questions.explanation: Legitimate svchost.exe runs strictly from C:\Windows\System32; running from AppData indicates malware. lsass.exe without a Microsoft signature abusing CPU is process spoofing. Encoded PowerShell commands signify fileless malicious script execution.

questions.question: Match the Windows management utility or location to its correct startup configuration function: (1) Task Manager (Startup Tab), (2) Services.msc, (3) Registry (HKCU\...\Run).
questions.explanation: Task Manager Startup tab manages user application startup impact; Services.msc controls service startup behavior; HKCU Run registry keys hold per-user automatic execution paths.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Match the Windows Defender Firewall rule parameter to its intended security outcome: (1) Block Inbound TCP Port 445, (2) Block Outbound TCP Port 25, (3) Allow Inbound TCP Port 3389.
questions.explanation: Port 445 controls SMB (ransomware mitigation); Port 25 controls outbound SMTP (spam mitigation); Port 3389 allows RDP connections.

questions.question: Match the Task Manager column indicator to its diagnostic role when evaluating suspicious malware behavior: (1) Image Path Name / File Location, (2) Digital Signature / Publisher, (3) Command Line Column.
questions.explanation: File Location checks system paths vs temp paths; Digital Signature verifies authenticity; Command Line reveals hidden switches/scripts.

questions.question: Match the suspicious startup persistence mechanism to the appropriate tool used to inspect and disable it: (1) Scheduled Tasks running unknown scripts at logon, (2) Malicious Windows Service set to start automatically, (3) Unknown browser extension launching on startup.
questions.explanation: Task Scheduler manages scheduled triggers; Services snap-in manages background system services; Browser extensions are controlled in web browser settings.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Match the firewall profile type in Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security to its corresponding network environment: (1) Domain Profile, (2) Private Profile, (3) Public Profile.
questions.explanation: Domain profile activates on AD networks; Private profile is for trusted home/work networks; Public profile enforces maximum protection on untrusted public Wi-Fi.

questions.question: Match each process status in Task Manager to the correct administrative remediation response: (1) Process status 'Not Responding' during malware activity, (2) Unsigned binary running from C:\Users\Public\Update.exe, (3) Legitimate Windows system process utilizing elevated CPU under normal load.
questions.explanation: Frozen/hung processes require End Task; executable binaries in public directories require isolation and deletion; normal system processes should be allowed to run.

questions.question: Match the command-line utility switch to its process termination task: (1) taskkill /IM malicious.exe /F, (2) taskkill /PID 4512 /F, (3) tasklist /FI "STATUS eq NOT RESPONDING".
questions.explanation: /IM specifies image name; /PID specifies process ID number; /FI applies filters such as status.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Match the Windows Defender Firewall Action setting to its behavior when matching traffic occurs: (1) Allow the connection, (2) Allow the connection if it is secure, (3) Block the connection.
questions.explanation: 'Allow' permits standard packets; 'Allow if secure' requires IPsec security association; 'Block' drops matching packets.

questions.question: Match the process anomaly visible in Task Manager Details tab to the corresponding type of attack: (1) Multiple duplicate instances of conhost.exe running under a standard user account, (2) High network utilization by an unknown background process to remote IP addresses on Port 6667, (3) Constant high CPU/GPU utilization by an idle desktop system.
questions.explanation: Multiple unexpected conhost processes indicate shell spawning; Port 6667 traffic indicates IRC botnet beaconing; 100% idle system utilization signals unauthorized cryptomining.

questions.question: Match the step of the CompTIA 7-step Malware Removal Procedure to its correct action during process isolation: (1) Step 2: Isolate the infected system, (2) Step 3: Disable System Restore, (3) Step 4: Remediate the infected system.
questions.explanation: Step 2 is Isolation (disconnect network); Step 3 is Disabling System Restore; Step 4 is Remediation (malware removal and cleanup).

questions.question: Match the Task Manager tab to its diagnostic function when investigating computer performance and security: (1) Details Tab, (2) Services Tab, (3) Startup App Tab.
questions.explanation: Details tab shows process execution parameters (PID, user, memory); Services tab lists system services; Startup App tab manages auto-start applications.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Match the Windows Defender Firewall Rule type to the criteria used for filtering network traffic: (1) Program Rule, (2) Port Rule, (3) Custom Rule.
questions.explanation: Program rules filter by executable path; Port rules filter by TCP/UDP ports; Custom rules combine multiple parameters including IP ranges and protocols.

questions.question: Match the registry run key location to its persistence behavior for startup programs: (1) HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...\Run, (2) HKEY_CURRENT_USER\...\Run, (3) HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...\RunOnce.
questions.explanation: HKLM Run applies to all system users; HKCU Run applies only to the active user; RunOnce executes a single time and self-deletes.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Match the firewall configuration goal to the appropriate administrative tool: (1) Quick toggle to enable/disable firewall across public/private profiles, (2) Granular creation of inbound/outbound rules based on IP address ranges, (3) Command-line script to reset firewall rules to installation defaults.
questions.explanation: Basic Control Panel applet provides simple toggles; wf.msc allows complex custom rule creation; netsh CLI resets firewall defaults.

questions.question: Match each suspicious process name anomaly to its correct detection analysis: (1) csrsss.exe running alongside csrss.exe, (2) System Idle Process consuming 95% CPU, (3) explorer.exe running under system user account 'SYSTEM'.
questions.explanation: csrsss.exe (extra 's') is typosquatting; System Idle Process CPU usage represents unused capacity; Windows Explorer running as SYSTEM indicates privilege escalation or spoofing.

questions.question: Match the Task Manager startup impact rating to its operational definition: (1) High Impact, (2) Low Impact, (3) Disabled.
questions.explanation: High Impact delays boot noticeably; Low Impact has minimal resource usage; Disabled prevents automatic boot execution.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Match the netsh command to its firewall management function: (1) netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off, (2) netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state on, (3) netsh advfirewall show allprofiles.
questions.explanation: 'state off' disables firewall; 'state on' enables firewall; 'show allprofiles' displays current operational status.

questions.question: Match the persistence method used by malware to its recommended remediation step: (1) Malicious DLL injected into a legitimate system process, (2) Unauthorized scheduled task configured to execute every 60 minutes, (3) Rogue Windows Service set to Automatic startup.
questions.explanation: Injected DLLs require terminating host process and scanning in Safe Mode; malicious tasks are deleted in Task Scheduler; rogue services are disabled in services.msc.

questions.objective: 2.2 Local Security Settings and OS Security
questions.question: Match the host firewall rule direction to the network scenario requiring it: (1) Inbound Rule, (2) Outbound Rule.
questions.explanation: Inbound rules filter incoming connections initiated outside the computer; Outbound rules filter outgoing connections originating from the local host.

questions.objective: 2.3 Supporting Web Browsers and OS Security
questions.question: Ticket Note: Multiple end users report receiving 'NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID' warnings when accessing internal web applications. Inspection shows the local system clocks are offset by 3 hours due to a failed domain synchronization. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Resync local system time with the NTP server
B) Export and import the root CA certificate into Trusted Root Store
C) Disable HTTPS scanning in the local host firewall
D) Clear the web browser SSL slate and cache
questions.explanation: Invalid certificate date errors across multiple users caused by local clock skew are resolved by resynchronizing the client time with the Network Time Protocol (NTP) domain server.

questions.question: Ticket Note: An office worker reports that printing print jobs results in blank pages coming out of an network laser printer. The toner cartridge was recently replaced. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Remove the protective sealing tape from the toner cartridge
B) Restart the Print Spooler service on the local workstation
C) Calibrate the fuser assembly temperature in printer settings
questions.explanation: Blank pages from a newly replaced laser toner cartridge typically occur when the protective sealing tape covering the toner roller was not pulled out prior to installation.

questions.question: Ticket Note: An administrator reviews a BSOD crash dump using WinDbg. The bugcheck analysis highlights 'DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL' pointing directly to 'nvlddmkm.sys'. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Roll back or update the graphics card driver
C) Execute chkdsk /f /r on the primary boot volume
D) Increase virtual memory paging file size
questions.explanation: 'nvlddmkm.sys' is the Nvidia display driver. DRIVER_IRQL errors associated with a specific driver file require updating, rolling back, or clean re-installing that display driver.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Print jobs sent to a shared network printer sit in the queue with status 'Printing' indefinitely, blocking all subsequent user jobs. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Stop the Print Spooler service, clear %systemroot%\System32\Spool\PRINTERS, and restart Spooler
B) Replace the network Ethernet patch cable attached to the printer
C) Reinstall the printer driver using generic Windows drivers
D) Factory reset the printer network card via web management console
questions.explanation: Stuck print spooler queues are resolved by stopping the Print Spooler service, purging corrupt pending spool files from the PRINTERS folder, and restarting the service.

questions.question: Ticket Note: User reports pop-up advertisements appearing on the desktop even when browser windows are closed. Task Manager reveals a process running from 'C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\adrun.exe'. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Isolate the workstation from the network and run an anti-malware scan
B) Clear the browser cookies and browsing history
C) Block inbound TCP port 80 on the host firewall
D) Run sfc /scannow in elevated command prompt
questions.explanation: Adware running executable processes out of user temp folders requires immediate network isolation to prevent lateral spread, followed by full malware remediation.

questions.question: Ticket Note: End user cannot connect to internal shares. IPConfig shows IP address 169.254.43.12 with subnet mask 255.255.0.0. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Troubleshoot connectivity to the DHCP server or verify IP scope exhaustion
B) Configure static DNS server addresses on the workstation interface
C) Replace the network interface card (NIC)
D) Enable netbios over TCP/IP in IPv4 properties
questions.explanation: An APIPA address (169.254.x.x) indicates the client failed to contact a DHCP server or the server pool is out of available IP addresses.

questions.question: Ticket Note: User reports system slowdown and crash dumps with 'CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED'. System File Checker reports corrupt files that could not be repaired. What is the precise resolution?
options: B) Run bootrec /fixmbr from Recovery Console
D) Re-register DLL files using regsvr32
questions.explanation: When SFC fails to fix corrupt system files, DISM (Deployment Image Servicing and Management) repairs the underlying Windows component store using Windows Update or source images.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Printed pages from a laser printer exhibit dark vertical black streaks running down the entire page. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Replace the drum unit or clean the primary corona wire
C) Lower the print resolution setting in print preferences
D) Clean the printer ink cartridges with alcohol
questions.explanation: Continuous vertical lines or streaks on laser printouts are caused by scratches on the photosensitive drum unit or a dirty corona wire.

questions.objective: 2.3 Supporting Web Browsers and OS Security
questions.question: Ticket Note: User gets a 'Certificate Name Mismatch' error when navigating to 'https://mail.company.com'. The certificate subject name lists 'legacy-mail.company.com'. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Update the SSL/TLS certificate on the server to include the current domain name/SAN
B) Change the client DNS setting to point to 8.8.8.8
C) Add an inbound rule in Windows Defender Firewall for TCP port 443
D) Flush the local DNS cache using ipconfig /flushdns
questions.explanation: A certificate name mismatch occurs when the URL accessed does not match the Subject Name or Subject Alternative Name (SAN) configured on the server SSL certificate.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Mobile user states smartphone battery drains rapidly and device gets warm to touch even when idle. Diagnostic logs show constant background location requests. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Review location permissions and revoke access for unnecessary background apps
B) Perform a factory hard reset of the smartphone operating system
C) Replace the device SIM card
D) Calibrate the device screen brightness
questions.explanation: Rapid battery drain and thermal issues caused by constant location monitoring are resolved by restricting background location privileges for rogue or misconfigured apps.

questions.question: Ticket Note: User reports error 'The operational system could not be loaded because a required file is missing or contains errors: \Windows\System32\winload.efi'. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Boot to Windows Recovery Environment and run bootrec /rebuildbcd
B) Replace the primary RAM modules
C) Convert the disk partition structure from GPT to MBR
D) Restore the BIOS configuration to default settings
questions.explanation: Missing winload.efi or BCD corruption during boot requires launching WinRE command prompt and executing bootrec /rebuildbcd to restore boot configuration data.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Paper jams occur frequently at the tray feeder of an office laser printer. Physical inspection shows worn and smooth rubber rollers. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Replace the paper pickup rollers / maintenance kit
B) Adjust the printer fuser temperature
C) Replace the transfer belt assembly
D) Reinstall the print queue driver on the server
questions.explanation: Smooth, worn rubber pickup rollers lose traction, causing persistent paper feed misfeeds and jams; replacing the pickup/feed rollers resolves the issue.

questions.question: Ticket Note: A developer cannot connect via SSH (Port 22) to a remote Linux instance from their Windows host, receiving connection timeouts. Local network ping works. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Create an Outbound rule allowing TCP Port 22 in Windows Defender Firewall
B) Run netsh winsock reset on the local PC
C) Change the Ethernet cable connecting the computer
D) Disable Network Discovery on the Windows PC
questions.explanation: Timeout on specific application protocols while ping succeeds points to local or host firewall blocking outbound communication on that port (TCP 22).

questions.question: Ticket Note: Server OS logs show S.M.A.R.T Error: 'Reallocated Sectors Count exceeding threshold'. User experiences intermittent system freezes. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Immediately back up data and replace the hard drive
B) Run defragmenter on the affected drive volume
C) Reformat the drive using exFAT file system
D) Reseat the SATA power and data cables
questions.explanation: S.M.A.R.T reallocated sector warnings signal impending hardware failure of the disk drive. The immediate resolution is data backup and drive replacement.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Windows workstation experiences crash dumps with code 'PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA'. Testing reveals memory address corruption. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Run Windows Memory Diagnostic and replace failing RAM stick
B) Increase disk space allocation on C: drive
C) Update the system BIOS graphics settings
D) Reinstall the motherboard chipset drivers
questions.explanation: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA typically indicates defective physical RAM or severe driver fault referencing invalid memory locations. Testing/replacing RAM is the required resolution.

questions.question: Ticket Note: User can access websites using IP addresses (e.g., 1.1.1.1), but cannot navigate to site URLs (e.g., www.comptia.org). What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Update workstation DNS server settings to a valid address
B) Reset the local IPv4 Default Gateway address
C) Renew the DHCP IP address lease using ipconfig /renew
D) Replace the patch cable with a Crossover cable
questions.explanation: Successful navigation by IP address paired with failure by hostname confirms a DNS resolution failure.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Ransomware alert triggered on a Finance computer. User files are acquiring '.locked' extensions and ransom notes are generating. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Immediately disconnect the Ethernet network cable and disable Wi-Fi
B) Pay the requested cryptocurrency ransom
C) Run System Restore to revert back 2 days
D) Execute chkdsk /f to fix damaged sectors
questions.explanation: According to the CompTIA 7-step malware removal procedure, the immediate first step upon discovering active ransomware is isolating the infected system from the network.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Thermal receipt printer outputs paper, but printed receipts are completely blank. The roll was recently replaced by staff. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Flip or reload the thermal paper roll to face the correct side toward the printhead
B) Replace the thermal printer ribbon
C) Increase the thermal heating element voltage in properties
D) Clean the corona wire with isopropyl alcohol
questions.explanation: Thermal paper is coated with chemical dye on one side only. Installing the paper roll backwards results in totally blank receipts.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Workstation displays 'Operating System Not Found' at boot. BIOS/UEFI utility indicates boot order prioritizes USB external drive before internal SSD. USB flash drive is attached. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Remove the USB drive and adjust boot order priority in BIOS
B) Reinstall Windows OS on the SSD
C) Replace the internal SSD disk drive
D) Run diskpart clean on the internal SSD
questions.explanation: 'OS Not Found' when non-bootable USB drives are attached is resolved by removing the USB device and setting the primary internal storage drive first in boot sequence.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Desktop PC turns off unexpectedly after 10 minutes of high CPU usage. System logs show CPU temperature reaching 105C prior to shutdown. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Clean dust from heatsink, apply fresh thermal paste, and verify cooler mounting
B) Replace the power supply unit (PSU)
C) Upgrade system RAM to higher frequency
D) Flash system BIOS to newest firmware
questions.explanation: Thermal shutdowns caused by CPU overheating require thermal management: clearing dust, re-applying thermal paste, and ensuring the heatsink fan functions.

questions.objective: 2.3 Supporting Web Browsers and OS Security
questions.question: Ticket Note: Users report 'Untrusted Root Certificate' warnings when opening company HTTPS intranet sites. Local certificates are issued by internal enterprise CA. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Deploy the Internal Root CA Certificate to client Trusted Root Certification Authorities store
B) Disable TLS 1.3 in internet options
C) Add site IP to the local hosts file
D) Change web server port from 443 to 80
questions.explanation: Browsers flag untrusted root warnings for internal PKI certificates if the Enterprise Root CA certificate hasn't been imported into the client's Trusted Root store.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Printouts from an inkjet printer have missing horizontal lines and faded colors despite full ink tanks. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Perform a printhead cleaning utility routine from printer maintenance menu
C) Clear the Windows print spooler
questions.explanation: Faded colors and missing horizontal lines in inkjet output indicate clogged nozzles in the printhead, resolved by executing automated printhead cleaning routines.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Mobile user reports corporate email app crashes immediately upon opening. Other apps work normally. App update was installed last night. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Clear application cache/data or reinstall the application
C) Perform factory data reset on mobile device
questions.explanation: Isolated app crashes following an update are fixed by clearing app data/cache or performing a clean uninstallation and reinstallation of the application.

questions.question: Ticket Note: User reports intermittent network connectivity. Cable tester reveals wire pairs 1 and 3 are swapped on an RJ45 termination. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Re-terminate the cable ends using standard T568B wiring pinout on both ends
B) Enable auto-MDIX on the desktop network adapter settings
C) Replace the network switch with a managed switch
D) Change IP configuration from DHCP to static
questions.explanation: Miswired pins (wire swaps) cause crosstalk and link instability. Re-terminating connectors correctly to T568B standard resolves physical layer defects.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Windows updates repeatedly fail to install with error 0x800f081f. Windows Update Troubleshooter failed to fix the problem. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Reset Windows Update components and clear %systemroot%\SoftwareDistribution folder
B) Format the primary hard drive
D) Disable Windows Defender Antivirus permanently
questions.explanation: Persistent Windows Update failure codes are commonly solved by stopping update services and clearing corrupted update download caches in SoftwareDistribution.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Laser printer output smudges easily when touched; black toner wipes off the paper easily. What is the precise resolution?
options: B) Replace the primary charge roller
D) Decrease paper weight setting in driver
questions.explanation: Unfused toner that smudges off paper indicates the fuser assembly is not reaching adequate heat/pressure to permanently melt toner to paper fibers.

questions.question: Ticket Note: System infected with persistent rootkit malware. Antivirus scanning in standard mode fails to clean hidden files. System restore point is compromised. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Boot system from clean external recovery media and perform offline scan / OS rebuild
B) Run taskkill /f /im explorer.exe in standard desktop environment
C) Change user account password in Active Directory
D) Block port 443 outbound on host firewall
questions.explanation: Rootkits modify OS kernel binaries. Removal requires booting from a trusted offline recovery environment or performing a clean OS reinstall.

questions.question: Ticket Note: Monitor connected via DisplayPort displays 'No Signal'. Computer lights turn on and fans spin. Testing monitor on another PC works fine. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Reseat or replace the dedicated graphics card and verify power connections
B) Replace the display monitor backlight
questions.explanation: When the monitor is verified functional but receives no signal from PC host, the root cause is local display adapter (GPU) seating or failure.

questions.question: Ticket Note: User logs into Windows 11 PC and receives error: 'You've been logged in with a temporary profile'. Files on desktop are missing. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Fix profile SID key registry pointers under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList
B) Delete the user account folder from C:\Users
C) Re-join computer to local Workgroup
questions.explanation: Temporary profile errors stem from profile corruption in the Windows Registry. Removing the .bak extension on the profile SID key in ProfileList restores the main profile.

questions.question: Ticket Note: A RAID 5 array shows status 'Degraded' after a single hard drive failure indicator light turns amber. What is the precise resolution?
options: A) Replace the failed drive and initiate array rebuild
B) Back up data, delete RAID volume, and recreate array
C) Format the remaining drives using NTFS
D) Replace the RAID controller card immediately
questions.explanation: RAID 5 can tolerate a single disk failure. To restore redundancy from a degraded state, hot-swap/replace the failed disk and trigger a parity rebuild.

questions.objective: 2.3 Supporting Web Browsers and OS Security
